_comment: Risk Assessment Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor; pairs with SI (RA-5 vulnerability scans feed SI-2 flaw remediation), CM (RA-3 risk informs CM-3 change-impact), CA (RA-3 outputs are revisited at CA-2 / CA-7 cadence), and SR (RA-3(1) supply-chain risk is the entry point to the SR family). Smaller, methodology-heavy family — moderate baseline pulls 6 base controls plus 4 enhancements but the engineering work is process documentation, not tooling sprawl.
title: Risk Assessment Plan
description: Documents how the system categorizes information, identifies threats and vulnerabilities, assesses likelihood and impact, responds to risk, performs criticality analysis, and conducts threat hunting. Covers the controls of the RA family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with FIPS 199 (Categorization), FIPS 200 (Minimum Security Requirements), NIST SP 800-30 r1 (Risk Assessment Guide), NIST SP 800-37 r2 (RMF), NIST SP 800-39 (Managing Information Security Risk), and NIST SP 800-161 r1 (Supply Chain Risk Management).
intro_template:
This Risk Assessment Plan documents the risk-assessment approach for {system_name}. It establishes the methodology, tooling, cadences, and roles used to categorize information, identify threats and vulnerabilities, assess likelihood and impact, decide on risk response, perform criticality analysis on system components, and hunt for previously undetected threats.

The scope covers FIPS 199 / FIPS 200 categorization, system risk assessment per NIST SP 800-30 r1, vulnerability scanning per RA-5, organizational risk response per RA-7, supply-chain criticality per RA-9 and RA-3(1), and proactive threat hunting per RA-10 within the {system_name} authorization boundary. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (Risk Assessment family), NIST SP 800-30 r1 (Risk Assessment Guide), NIST SP 800-39 (Managing Information Security Risk), and NIST SP 800-161 r1 (Supply Chain Risk Management).
approach_template:
{system_name} categorizes information per FIPS 199 using {categorization_method}. Risk assessment follows {risk_methodology} on the cadence in §4.3, with results recorded in {risk_register_location}. Vulnerability scanning is performed by {vuln_scan_tool} on the cadence in §4.5; findings flow into the SI-2 remediation queue. Threat-hunt activity is performed {threat_hunt_cadence} by {threat_hunt_role}.

Additional details on categorization, risk-assessment methodology, risk-register management, vulnerability scanning, risk response, criticality analysis, supply-chain risk, threat hunting, and privacy risk are captured in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Risk-assessment performance for {system_name} is tracked through the metrics in §6.1 (open vs closed risks, mean time to risk decision, vulnerability scan coverage, KEV-affected scan-coverage rate, high-criticality component count, threat-hunt findings closed). The risk register is reviewed on the cadence in §6.2; new risks are entered as discovered (RA-3 baseline assumption is a continuous activity, not a one-time exercise). Risk-monitoring reports feed the CA-7 continuous-monitoring strategy and surface to the AO at the cadence required by RA-3.
integration_template: This Risk Assessment Plan does not stand alone. The SI family consumes RA-5 vulnerability data via SI-2 flaw remediation; the CM family consumes RA-3 outputs to inform CM-3 change-impact analysis and CM-4 security-impact analysis; the CA family revisits risk at CA-2 assessment and CA-7 continuous monitoring; the SR family extends RA-3(1) and RA-9 into formal supply-chain risk management; the IR family escalates incidents to revisit risk decisions; the AO consumes the risk register for the authorization decision. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where RA-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

commonly_inheritable_controls.from: Enterprise threat-hunting program (when shared SOC / hunt team)

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: Methodology references and tooling that anchor the rest of the plan.

questions.label: Categorization method (one-liner)
questions.help: How information is categorized per FIPS 199 (e.g., 'FIPS 199 + CNSSI 1253 overlay', 'FIPS 199 with NIST SP 800-60 v2 information-type guide').

questions.label: Risk-assessment methodology
questions.help: Methodology used to assess risk (e.g., 'NIST SP 800-30 r1 likelihood × impact', 'OCTAVE Allegro', 'FAIR (quantitative)').

questions.label: Risk register location
questions.help: Where the risk register is maintained (e.g., 'GRC tool — Archer / ServiceNow GRC', 'eMASS', 'Spreadsheet under /repo/risk/register.xlsx with version control').

questions.label: Vulnerability scanning tool
questions.help: Primary scanner (typically the same tool referenced in the SI plan: e.g., 'Tenable.sc', 'Qualys VMDR', 'Rapid7 InsightVM').

questions.label: Threat-hunt cadence
questions.help: How often proactive hunts are conducted (e.g., 'Quarterly hypothesis-driven hunts; continuous SOAR-assisted micro-hunts').

questions.label: Threat-hunt role
questions.help: Role that performs hunts (e.g., 'Enterprise SOC Threat Intelligence Team', 'External MDR retainer + internal IR lead').

questions.label: FIPS 199 categorization (CIA triad)
questions.help: The Confidentiality / Integrity / Availability impact levels (Low / Moderate / High) and how they were determined. Reference NIST SP 800-60 v2 information-type guide for the rationale.

questions.label: High-water-mark rationale
questions.help: Per FIPS 199, system categorization is the high-water mark across information types. Document the deciding information type and any moderation per CNSSI 1253 if applicable.

questions.label: Impact-level prioritization (RA-2(1))
questions.help: Per RA-2(1), how individual data elements within an information type are prioritized when impact varies. Often required at moderate / high baselines.

questions.label: Re-categorization triggers
questions.help: What events cause categorization to be revisited (e.g., 'Significant change per CM-4', 'New information type onboarded', 'Annual ATO review').

family_questions.label: Risk-Assessment Methodology (RA-3)
family_questions.description: How likelihood, impact, and risk are computed.

questions.label: Likelihood scale
options: Qualitative 5-tier (Very Low / Low / Moderate / High / Very High)
Hybrid (qualitative for unknown, quantitative for measured)

questions.label: Impact scale
options: Qualitative 5-tier (Very Low / Low / Moderate / High / Very High)

questions.label: Risk-assessment cadence (RA-3 ODV)
questions.help: How often the system risk assessment is refreshed. RA-3 ODV — common values: 'Annually + on significant change', 'Every 3 years + on significant change'.

questions.label: Risk-assessment results distribution (RA-3 ODV)
questions.help: Roles / personnel to whom risk-assessment results are distributed (System Owner, ISSO, ISSM, AO, ITRM committee, etc.).

questions.label: Risk-assessment documentation format
questions.help: Format / template used (e.g., 'NIST SP 800-30 r1 Appendix L worksheets', 'Internal Risk Assessment Report template', 'eMASS-generated Security Assessment Report').

family_questions.label: Risk Register Management
family_questions.description: How identified risks are tracked, prioritized, and aged.

questions.label: Risk aging policy
questions.help: How long risks may sit at each status before re-evaluation (e.g., 'Open risks reviewed quarterly; accepted risks re-validated annually; mitigated risks closed when controls verified').

questions.label: Escalation thresholds
questions.help: Thresholds at which risks escalate beyond System Owner (e.g., 'High residual → ISSM brief; Very High residual → AO immediate notification').

family_questions.label: Vulnerability Scanning (RA-5)
family_questions.description: Scan scope, cadence, and coordination with SI-2 remediation.

questions.label: Scan cadence
questions.help: Cadence by scope (e.g., 'External: continuous; Internal authenticated: weekly; Container images: on build; Web app DAST: monthly'). RA-5 ODV.

questions.label: Authenticated vs unauthenticated
questions.help: Posture on authenticated scans (preferred for accuracy). Service-account credential management.

questions.label: Vulnerability information update mechanism (RA-5(2))
questions.help: How scanner signatures are kept current (auto-update, daily plugin pulls). Required by RA-5(2) — system is scanned with current information.

questions.label: Findings routing
questions.help: Where scan findings land. Typically a remediation queue feeding SI-2. Severity classification mapping.

questions.label: Information sharing (RA-5(11))
questions.help: Per RA-5(11), how vulnerability information is shared with stakeholders (System Owner, ISSO, ISSM, downstream consumers, partner systems).

questions.label: Privileged-access controls for scanners (RA-5(5))
questions.help: Per RA-5(5), how scanner privileged access is controlled. Service-account vault, JIT credential, MFA on scanner console.

family_questions.label: Risk Response (RA-7)
family_questions.description: Decision framework and authority for risk disposition.

questions.label: Risk-acceptance authority by tier
questions.help: Who can accept risk at each level (e.g., 'Low: System Owner; Moderate: ISSM; High: AO; Very High: AO with CIO concurrence'). Reference any organizational risk-tolerance statement.

questions.label: Risk-acceptance evidence required
questions.help: Documentation required for risk acceptance (e.g., 'Signed risk-acceptance memo + entry in risk register + POA&M for periodic re-validation').

questions.label: Accepted-risk revisit cadence
questions.help: How often accepted risks are re-validated to ensure conditions haven't changed.

family_questions.label: Criticality Analysis (RA-9)
family_questions.description: Identification of critical components for prioritized protection.

questions.label: Criticality-analysis methodology
questions.help: Approach to identifying critical components (e.g., 'NIST SP 800-161 r1 § 2.4 supply-chain criticality; NIST SP 800-30 r1 Appendix F asset value; FMEA for failure-impact analysis').

questions.label: Critical-component categories
options: Database servers holding CUI / PII / PHI

questions.label: Criticality-analysis review cadence
questions.help: How often the analysis is refreshed (e.g., 'Annual + on architecture change').

questions.label: How criticality informs decisions
questions.help: How criticality drives architecture choices, redundancy investments, monitoring prioritization, supplier vetting depth.

family_questions.label: Supply Chain Risk (RA-3(1))
family_questions.description: Supply-chain-specific risk assessment, separate from generic RA-3.

questions.label: Critical supply-chain dependencies
questions.help: Vendors / components whose compromise would disable the system. Single-source items, foreign-sourced components per FAR / DFARS, key open-source projects.

questions.label: Assessment inputs used
options: Open-source project health (commits, maintainers, vulnerability history)

questions.label: Handoff to SR (Supply Chain Risk Management) family
questions.help: How RA-3(1) outputs feed the SR family controls. If SR plan exists, reference its location.

family_questions.label: Threat Hunting (RA-10)
family_questions.description: Proactive search for previously undetected threats.

questions.label: Hunt methodology
questions.help: Hypothesis-driven hunts based on threat intelligence, MITRE ATT&CK techniques, anomaly-driven hunts. Tooling (SIEM, EDR query, custom queries).

questions.label: Hunt-finding handling
questions.help: What happens when a hunt finds something (incident escalation per IR plan, control gap → POA&M, detection-rule creation feeding SI-4).

family_questions.label: Privacy Risk Assessment (RA-8)
family_questions.description: Privacy Impact Assessment if applicable to information categorization.

questions.label: PIA required by categorization
options: Yes — system handles PII (PIA required + published)
Yes — PIA required + not published (operational sensitivity)
No — system does not handle PII

questions.label: PIA methodology
questions.help: Methodology used (e.g., 'NIST IR 8062 privacy risk model', 'OMB M-03-22 PIA template', 'Internal privacy-impact framework based on FIPPs').

questions.label: PIA review cadence
questions.help: When PIA is refreshed (e.g., 'Annually; on significant change to information collection or use'). Reference PT family if authored.

family_questions.label: Risk-Assessment Scope and Coverage
family_questions.description: Quantitative scope numbers that anchor metrics later in the plan.

questions.label: Open risks in register (approximate)
questions.help: Order-of-magnitude count to anchor the metric tracking.

questions.label: System components in scope of RA-5
questions.help: Approximate count of hosts / containers / images covered by vulnerability scans.

questions.label: Critical components per RA-9 analysis
questions.help: Count of components classified as critical.

questions.label: Third-party / supply-chain dependencies tracked
questions.help: Count of vendors / open-source projects in the supply-chain register.

family_questions.label: Risk-Assessment Metrics & KPIs
family_questions.description: Metrics tracked to demonstrate RA control effectiveness.

questions.label: Tracked metrics
suggestions: Mean time to risk decision (Identified → Decision)
% Accepted risks reviewed within revisit cadence
Vulnerability scan coverage rate (% of in-scope assets scanned)
% Critical / High vulnerabilities patched within SLA (overlaps SI-2)
Supply-chain assessments completed within trigger cadence
Open POA&M items linked to RA controls

family_questions.label: Scan Coverage Verification
family_questions.description: How the org continuously verifies RA-5 scanning is correctly deployed.

questions.label: Scan-coverage reconciliation cadence
questions.help: How often the asset inventory (CMDB) is reconciled against scanned-asset roster. Detects shadow / unscanned hosts.

questions.label: Scanner signature-currency verification
questions.help: How the org verifies scan signatures are current (e.g., 'Daily plugin-update verification report'). Required by RA-5(2).

family_questions.label: Cross-references to other RMF artifacts
family_questions.description: Where this plan plugs into the broader RMF package.

questions.label: SSP section reference
questions.help: Where in the SSP the RA control implementations are summarized (e.g., 'SSP §13.11').

questions.label: POA&M ID prefix for RA findings
questions.help: Convention for RA-related POA&M items (e.g., 'POAM-RA-' for general; 'POAM-RA5-' for vuln-specific).

questions.label: SI-2 flaw-remediation consumer handoff
questions.help: How RA-5 findings flow into the SI-2 remediation queue. Tooling, ticket-creation automation, owner assignment.

questions.label: CM-4 security-impact analysis handoff
questions.help: How RA-3 outputs inform CM-4 / CM-3 change-impact analysis. Reference the CM Plan.

questions.label: CA-7 continuous-monitoring strategy reference
questions.help: Pointer to the CA-7 monitoring strategy document tying RA continuous-monitoring metrics to the broader ConMon plan.

questions.label: IR escalation handoff
questions.help: How incidents trigger risk-register revisits. Closed incidents that introduced new risk get entries in the register.

questions.label: SR family pointer
questions.help: Pointer to the SR (Supply Chain Risk Management) plan if authored. RA-3(1) is the gateway control; SR formalizes the program.

glossary.definition: A risk that the organization has formally chosen not to mitigate, having documented the rationale and approval. Subject to RA-7 revisit cadence.
Annualized Loss Expectancy — quantitative risk metric: ALE = SLE × ARO. Used in quantitative risk-assessment methodologies.
Annualized Rate of Occurrence — expected frequency of a threat event per year.
Per FIPS 199, the assignment of Low / Moderate / High impact ratings to a system based on the worst-case impact for confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability — the three security objectives evaluated for impact in FIPS 199 categorization.
Per RA-9, the process of identifying components whose failure or compromise would have the greatest mission impact, used to prioritize protective measures.
Factor Analysis of Information Risk — a quantitative risk-assessment methodology based on probabilistic loss-magnitude estimation.
Failure Mode and Effects Analysis — engineering technique for analyzing how a component can fail and the resulting impact.
Per FIPS 199, the highest impact level across all information types within a system. The system inherits this level as its overall categorization.
A theory of attacker behavior that drives a threat hunt (e.g., 'an attacker with our recently-disclosed credentials would attempt lateral movement to our database tier').
Per NIST SP 800-30 r1, the magnitude of harm from a threat event. Combined with likelihood to produce risk.
A category of information for FIPS 199 categorization (e.g., 'Personnel Management', 'System Development'). Per NIST SP 800-60 v2.
The level of risk before any controls / mitigations are applied. Compare with residual risk.
Known Exploited Vulnerabilities — CISA's catalog of CVEs known to be actively exploited; subject to BOD 22-01 federal remediation timelines.
Per NIST SP 800-30 r1, the probability that a threat event will occur and result in adverse impact. Combined with impact to produce risk.
A knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques based on real-world observations. Used to organize threat-hunting and detection-engineering programs.
Operationally Critical Threat, Asset, and Vulnerability Evaluation — a risk-assessment methodology developed at CMU SEI.
Privacy Impact Assessment — per RA-8, an analysis of how PII is collected, used, shared, maintained, and disposed of.
The risk that remains after controls and mitigations are applied. Subject to risk-response decisions per RA-7.
Per NIST SP 800-30 r1, a measure of the extent to which an entity is threatened by a potential circumstance, expressed as a function of likelihood and impact.
A document or system tracking identified risks, their assessment, treatment decisions, owners, and review cadence.
Per RA-7, the chosen action for each identified risk: accept, mitigate, transfer, avoid, or share.
Software Bill of Materials — formal record of components in software. Used in supply-chain risk assessment per RA-3(1).
Single Loss Expectancy — quantitative loss from a single occurrence of a threat event. SLE × ARO = ALE.
Per RA-10, the proactive search through environments for adversary activity that has evaded existing detection. Driven by hypothesis or anomaly.
An entity or condition with the potential to cause harm. NIST SP 800-30 r1 categorizes them as adversarial, accidental, structural, or environmental.
Per NIST SP 800-30 r1, a weakness in a system, control, or implementation that could be exploited by a threat source.
